newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded generally lower on moderate to fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings on Choice product.

Retail demand continued fairly good for immediate post holiday needs, but at lower prices for most all Choice cuts. Choice rib and loin cuts continue to trade lower, with light demand for the immediate retail and HRI needs, consequently putting middle meats items under continual downward pressure for both immediate and post holiday needs.
Select cuts, generally steady, during most of the trading week, with a few credit items continuing to be under pressure.

Closely trimmed items followed some what the same pattern, the Choice cuts continued under the most downward pressure, sharply lower, and the Select cuts were generally steady. Beef trimmings traded firm on light to moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

The carcass price equivalent index value of a Choice 1-3 550-700 lbs carcass down 6.51 at 99.48; 700-850 lbs down 5.96 at 97.53; Select 1-3 550-700 lbs down 2.40 at 87.86; 700-850 lbs down 2.49 at 85.67.

For the week Select and Choice rib primal .50 to 5.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 5.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal steady to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 5.50 lower; Closely trimmed items steady to 4.00 lower; Beef trimmings 1.50 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 4.40 at 105.08; 700/850 Dn 3.85 at 104.13; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .29 at 93.46; 700/850 Dn .38 at 92.27.
The boneless beef market traded lower again this week as the supplies and offerings were too great for existing demand.

On the supply side, because of the continued fall runs, the cow slaughter numbers stayed at seasonally high levels. Meanwhile, demand became light as inventories swelled and the market channels filled up. In addition, Cutter cow carcasses traded lower as supplies mounted with an over abundance of leaner cows coming to market.

Moreover, cow cuts supplies were also plentiful, and most items traded at weak price levels. Utility carcasses steady; Cutter 1.50 lower; Fresh 90% boneless beef 3.00-3.50 lower; 85% 1.00-1.50 lower; 75% 1.00-2.50 lower; 65% steady. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, December 12, 1996 was estimated at 62.95 per cwt., down 1.75 from a week ago Friday.
